questions.stem: In FortiNAC-F global-object synchronization, which system is authoritative for shared objects?
choices: The endpoint supplicant
The managed CA's local database row
FortiNAC Manager
The switch's RADIUS client table
feedback: The supplicant is not a configuration authority for FortiNAC global objects.
Managed CA global objects are read-only and are overwritten from the Manager.
Correct: FortiNAC Manager owns the shared global-object configuration.
The switch RADIUS table is unrelated to Manager object replication.

questions.stem: A managed CA's Group row ID differs from the Manager's row ID, but the GUID matches. What should the engineer conclude?
choices: Different local row IDs are normal; the shared GUID identifies the global object
The objects are duplicates and both must be deleted
The managed CA is running the wrong VRRP group
The Manager must use the CA's local row ID
feedback: Correct: local database IDs are appliance-local; the GUID is the cross-appliance identity.
Different row IDs alone do not prove duplication and deleting global objects is unsafe.
VRRP group configuration has no relationship to FortiNAC object identity.
The Manager remains authoritative; local IDs do not need to match.

questions.stem: Which objects are examples of FortiNAC-F global synchronization content?
choices: Live packet captures and interface counters
Only local host MAC learning tables
Only AP radio channel assignments
Groups, Roles, Admin Profiles, and endpoint compliance objects
feedback: Packet captures and counters are operational evidence, not the listed global configuration objects.
Host propagation is a separate replication function from global-object synchronization.
AP radio channels are not the listed FortiNAC-F global objects.
Correct: the guide lists Groups, Roles, Admin Profiles, and compliance objects.

questions.stem: A GUID conflict is confirmed for one global Group on a managed CA. What is the safe repair posture?
choices: Run a broad UPDATE on every Group row
Back up, compare Manager/CA identity, and change only the stale managed-CA GUID under Support guidance
Change the Manager GUID to match the CA local ID
Delete all local-only groups before synchronizing
feedback: A broad update can damage valid global and local-only objects.
Correct: back up, compare exact objects, and perform a narrowly scoped repair with Support guidance.
The Manager is authoritative; changing its GUID to a local ID reverses the authority model.
Local-only objects must not be altered as part of a global-object repair.

questions.stem: Which timing is documented for automatic global-object synchronization in FortiNAC-F vF 7.6.3+?
choices: Every ten minutes
Every ten seconds
Only during firmware upgrade
Only when a host changes VLAN
feedback: Correct: the Manager guide documents a ten-minute interval for global-object synchronization.
Ten seconds is not the documented interval.
Synchronization is a regular configured process, not limited to firmware upgrade.
Host VLAN movement is not the trigger for global-object replication.

questions.stem: A TACACS+ request reaches FortiAuthenticator, but the NAS sends authorization before authentication. What is the core issue?
choices: The user group lacks a VLAN ID
The server DNS suffix is missing
The NAS transaction order is incompatible with the supported authentication-first flow
The RADIUS shared secret is too short
feedback: VLAN assignment is not the core TACACS+ sequence issue.
DNS may affect reachability but does not change TACACS+ request ordering.
Correct: FortiAuthenticator does not provide an authorization-before-authentication mode for this flow.
A RADIUS shared secret is not the TACACS+ phase-order issue.

questions.stem: Before FortiAuthenticator accepts TACACS+ requests, what must exist?
choices: A FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC
A registered client assigned to a TACACS+ policy
An Azure Data Collection Rule
A FortiPAM secret template
feedback: VRRP is unrelated to TACACS+ client registration.
Correct: the TACACS+ device must be registered and assigned to a policy.
A DCR is an Azure log-ingestion object, not an authentication prerequisite.
FortiPAM secret templates do not configure FortiAuthenticator TACACS+.

questions.stem: Where does FortiAuthenticator expose TACACS+ service debug logs?
choices: System > SD-WAN > Health Check
FortiManager Install Preview
FortiAnalyzer Log Forwarding > Output Profile
The /debug/ page with TACACS+ selected as the service
feedback: SD-WAN health checks do not expose FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ logs.
Install Preview belongs to FortiManager device configuration deployment.
Output Profile is a FortiAnalyzer log-forwarding feature.
Correct: open /debug/ and select TACACS+ from the service dropdown.

questions.stem: What is the documented FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ limitation for two-factor authentication?
choices: Append the token to the password because challenge/response is unsupported
Use a browser SAML redirect after every command
Send the token as a RADIUS Tunnel-Private-Group-Id
Require a client certificate on every SSH command
feedback: Correct: FortiAuthenticator documents token-appended password entry because TACACS+ challenge/response is unsupported.
SAML redirects are not the documented TACACS+ 2FA method.
Tunnel-Private-Group-Id is a RADIUS VLAN attribute, not TACACS+ OTP handling.
A client certificate is not the stated TACACS+ 2FA mechanism.

questions.stem: Why inspect both TACACS+ authentication and authorization logs?
choices: They are the same event stored twice
Authorization always happens before authentication
Client registration, authentication, and command authorization are separate decision gates
The debug page records only failed DNS lookups
feedback: The stages have different outcomes and evidence, not merely duplicate records.
FortiAuthenticator's documented sequence does not support authorization-first behavior.
Correct: successful authentication can still be denied by a later authorization rule.
The TACACS+ debug page is for TACACS+ service evidence, not only DNS.

questions.stem: A FortiPAM REST request uses a client certificate and bearer token. What does each prove?
choices: Both prove only the user's password
The certificate proves API role membership; the token proves the EMS tag
The certificate and token are interchangeable methods
The certificate establishes endpoint trust; the bearer token authenticates the API user
feedback: A password is not what either artifact represents in this design.
The certificate is used for client trust; the token identifies the API user.
They are independent gates, not interchangeable alternatives.
Correct: device trust and API identity are separate controls.

questions.stem: FortiPAM ZTNA is enabled, but a managed endpoint cannot launch a protected secret. Which check is especially important?
choices: The endpoint and FortiPAM use the same EMS server and expected tag is present
The SD-WAN quota counter has reset
The FortiSwitch VRRP priority is 255
The FortiAnalyzer DCR table has TimeGenerated
feedback: Correct: FortiPAM tag control depends on the same EMS control plane and matching posture tag.
Quota counters do not determine FortiPAM secret access.
VRRP priority is unrelated to endpoint posture.
Azure table schema does not authorize a FortiPAM secret launch.

questions.stem: What does the /pam URL map in the FortiPAM access proxy do?
choices: It changes the API user's bearer token
It maps the incoming URL prefix to the pam-service API gateway
It creates the EMS endpoint tag automatically
It disables client certificate validation
feedback: The API token is generated for the API user and is not changed by URL mapping.
Correct: the API gateway maps /pam to the FortiPAM service.
EMS tags are created/evaluated by endpoint management, not URL maps.
Client certificate behavior is controlled separately in the access proxy.

questions.stem: A curl call succeeds only when -k is added. What is the safer production correction?
choices: Disable the FortiPAM API user
Remove the bearer token from the request
Install/trust the correct server CA and validate the TLS certificate chain
Set every EMS tag to allow
feedback: Disabling the API user removes identity rather than fixing TLS trust.
The bearer token is still required for API-user authentication.
Correct: -k bypasses server validation; fix the trust chain instead.
Allowing every tag weakens posture controls and does not fix TLS validation.

questions.stem: FortiPAM login succeeds but access to one secret is denied. Which control may still block the operation?
choices: The FortiSIEM offline repository mount
The FortiSwitch tracked destination
The Windows DNS priority list
Secret-level ZTNA posture or secret permission
feedback: The offline repo is unrelated to privileged secret authorization.
VRRP route tracking does not authorize a PAM secret.
DNS priority may affect name resolution, not the secret permission decision.
Correct: secret-level ZTNA and secret permissions are separate from appliance login.

questions.stem: For FortiSIEM 7.5.1 offline OS repository preparation, what storage requirement is documented?
choices: At least 2 TB on the mounted staging filesystem
At least 2 GB on the Supervisor root partition
A 375 GB temporary directory only
No local storage because the ZIP contains all OS packages
feedback: Correct: the 7.5.1 guide specifies at least 2 TB for the OS repository.
2 GB is far below the documented repository requirement.
375 GB belongs to earlier version documentation and must not be reused for 7.5.1.
The OS repository is a separate dependency from the main upgrade ZIP.

questions.stem: Why extract fsm-sync-os-repo.sh from the targeted upgrade package?
choices: The script configures FortiGate BGP neighbors
The script is version-specific and should match the upgrade package
The script creates a new RADIUS client secret
The script replaces the Supervisor database
feedback: The script builds the FortiSIEM OS repository, not BGP configuration.
Correct: the Community tip recommends extracting the script from the target version's upgrade RPM.
RADIUS client secrets are unrelated to repository synchronization.
The repository script does not replace the FortiSIEM database.

questions.stem: Which command tells the Supervisor upgrade to use the mounted offline repository?
choices: ./upgrade.sh --proxy-only /repo
./upgrade.sh --skip-database-check
./upgrade.sh --offline-osrepo-path /offline-repo
./upgrade.sh --disable-wget
feedback: The documented parameter is not a proxy-only option.
Skipping database checks is not the offline repository selector.
Correct: the guide documents --offline-osrepo-path with the mounted repository path.
Disabling wget is not how the upgrade script selects offline packages.

questions.stem: After Supervisor is upgraded, what extra value does a Worker upgrade consume?
choices: The FortiGate remote AS number
The FortiPAM API bearer token
The FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ shared secret
The offline repository OS update password from Supervisor
feedback: The BGP remote AS is unrelated to FortiSIEM Worker updates.
FortiPAM API credentials do not authorize FortiSIEM OS package access.
TACACS+ shared secrets do not participate in the Worker upgrade.
Correct: the Worker script uses the Supervisor's offline-repository OS update password.

questions.stem: Which order matches the documented FortiSIEM component dependencies?
choices: Supervisor/Manager first, then Workers, then Collectors
Collectors first, then Workers, then Supervisor
Workers first, then Manager, then repository staging
All components concurrently without a mounted repository
feedback: Correct: the guide upgrades Supervisor/Manager before Workers and then Collectors.
Collectors depend on the Supervisor image-server path and should not lead the sequence.
Workers require the upgraded Supervisor repository password and should not be first.
The offline procedure requires a complete mounted repository and staged order.

questions.stem: What is the Multi-Connect feature limitation documented for FortiClient?
choices: Only SSL VPN tunnels can connect concurrently
Only IPsec IKEv2 tunnels are eligible and the feature is beta
Only one tunnel can be configured per profile
It supports every tunnel protocol without version constraints
feedback: SSL VPN is not the documented eligible tunnel type for this beta feature.
Correct: the guide limits Multi-Connect to eligible IPsec IKEv2 tunnels and marks it beta.
The profile can list up to 50 eligible IKEv2 tunnels.
The feature has explicit tunnel-type and platform constraints.

questions.stem: What does DNS Priority control on Windows when Multi-Connect is enabled?
choices: Which tunnel receives all application traffic regardless of routing
Which tunnel is allowed to negotiate IKE first
The order of tunnel interfaces/DNS servers Windows tries for name queries
The FortiSASE PoP server certificate
feedback: DNS priority is not a general packet steering policy for every application flow.
IKE negotiation order is not what the DNS priority list configures.
Correct: Windows queries the DNS server on the highest-priority tunnel first, then tries the next if needed.
PoP certificate selection is unrelated to endpoint DNS resolver order.

questions.stem: A user reports the SASE tunnel is up but the on-prem tunnel is down. What is the right diagnostic approach?
choices: Assume the endpoint profile was not received
Edit the FortiSASE-owned Phase 1 and Phase 2 settings
Disable the SASE tunnel for every endpoint
Inspect each tunnel independently and validate the custom gateway's IKEv2 parameters
feedback: A working SASE tunnel suggests the profile may have reached the endpoint.
FortiSASE service-owned Phase 1/2 settings are not editable through that interface.
Disabling the SASE service is not a diagnosis of the separate custom tunnel.
Correct: SASE and custom IKEv2 tunnels have separate ownership and negotiation state.

questions.stem: Why must an on-prem gateway match the endpoint's custom-tunnel parameters?
choices: FortiSASE configures specific IKEv2 proposals and lifetimes on FortiClient
The gateway inherits the FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC
The custom tunnel uses the Azure DCR identifier as its peer ID
Windows DNS Priority rewrites the Phase 2 proposal
feedback: Correct: the tunnel settings guide lists endpoint parameters the remote gateway must match.
VRRP virtual MAC is not an IPsec proposal parameter.
DCR IDs belong to Azure log ingestion, not IKE identity.
DNS priority controls resolver order and does not rewrite IKE/Phase 2 negotiation.

questions.stem: Both tunnels are up, but an internal hostname resolves to the public answer. What should be inspected?
choices: FortiSIEM repository mount state
Windows DNS Priority order and each tunnel's DNS server
FortiSwitch VRRP destination tracking
FortiAnalyzer output-profile variables
feedback: The offline repository does not affect endpoint name resolution.
Correct: DNS priority maps to Windows tunnel interface metric and determines resolver order.
VRRP route tracking is not the endpoint's resolver selection control.
Azure output variables do not determine which DNS server Windows queries.

questions.stem: The FortiSASE tunnel's Phase 1/2 settings are not editable in the console. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The endpoint has lost its EMS tag
The tunnel is using SSL VPN instead of IKEv2
The SASE service owns those parameters; configure custom on-prem tunnels separately
The API bearer token has expired
feedback: An EMS tag issue affects posture/authorization, not tunnel-setting ownership.
Missing edit controls do not indicate a change in VPN protocol.
Correct: the Community clarification says SASE Phase 1/2 settings cannot be changed there.
API tokens are unrelated to service-owned IPsec parameters.

questions.stem: What is the key role of quota-limit on an SD-WAN member?
choices: It sets the interface MTU
It defines a monthly traffic-volume threshold in gigabytes
It forces the member physically down when the ISP link is up
It caps every packet to a fixed bandwidth rate
feedback: MTU is a separate interface setting.
Correct: quota-limit sets the volume threshold used for monthly overage steering.
The member can remain alive; the feature adjusts selection preference.
The quota feature is not a hard rate limiter or per-packet shaper.

questions.stem: Which command inspects quota/overage state for one SD-WAN member?
choices: diagnose sys sdwan bill member <id>
get router info vrrp
diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp
execute tacacs test user
feedback: Correct: FortiOS 8.0 adds the SD-WAN bill member diagnostic.
That command displays VRRP state, not billing counters.
The wireless controller command is not the quota diagnostic.
TACACS user testing is unrelated to SD-WAN member usage.

questions.stem: A member is over quota but traffic remains on it. What should be checked with billing output?
choices: Whether the BGP neighbor is in OpenConfirm
Whether the FortiPAM certificate is valid
Whether the billing counter is overaged and overage is enabled
Whether the FortiNAC EAP session has expired
feedback: BGP state does not establish the member's quota accounting state.
FortiPAM certificate validation does not affect SD-WAN quota counters.
Correct: verify threshold, billing start day, overage enablement, and current overaged state.
EAP session state is unrelated to SD-WAN member selection.

questions.stem: Why might quota steering not move a flow even when overage is enabled?
choices: The FortiGate must reboot at the billing boundary
The member must be removed from the routing table manually
The SD-WAN service ignores the configured eligible members and SLA
The alternate member is not alive or is excluded by the matching service
feedback: A reboot is not the documented requirement for the quota feature.
Manual route removal is not the intended steering mechanism.
The service rule and selection mode still determine which members can be selected.
Correct: an alternate must be alive and eligible in the matching service.

questions.stem: How can an engineer prove that a quota-driven path change affected actual packets?
choices: Compare service4/service6 selected members and capture the test flow's egress interface
Look only at quota-limit in configuration
Check whether the WAN interface has a green link LED
Review the FortiAnalyzer output-profile name
feedback: Correct: service state plus packet capture proves selected member and actual forwarding path.
Configuration shows intent, not that threshold was crossed or the flow moved.
A link LED proves physical link state, not SD-WAN service selection.
The output-profile name is unrelated to the packet's WAN egress.

questions.stem: What happens when the configured billing period resets?
choices: The SD-WAN member is permanently disabled
The usage counter and overage preference reset for the new billing period
All SLA targets are deleted
The FortiGate clears every session table
feedback: The feature is designed to resume normal preference after the billing period resets.
Correct: the example resets accumulated usage and overage preference on the next billing day.
SLA targets remain configured; the quota feature does not delete them.
The feature does not require clearing all firewall sessions.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes quota steering from health-check failover?
choices: Quota steering only applies when the physical interface is down
Health checks count monthly gigabytes while quota checks RTT
Quota changes member preference while the link may remain alive; health checks measure path quality
Both mechanisms are identical and share the same counter
feedback: The member can stay physically up while becoming less preferred due to usage.
Health checks measure reachability/performance, not monthly billing volume.
Correct: quota is a billing-volume input; health checks are path-quality inputs.
The mechanisms use different evidence and should be diagnosed separately.
